item.title: Research Assistant – China Studies (US-China Competition & Indo-Pacific)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 12/1/2026.

Note: 0–2 years of experience; previous internship experience strongly preferred. Salary $50,000–$54,000. Fully onsite in Washington, DC. Working proficiency in Mandarin Chinese required. Bachelor’s in East Asian studies, international relations, political science, history, public policy, or related field required. Stata/Excel required. Must submit resume, cover letter, transcripts, and 500-word writing sample on a topic related to the position. Apply at aei.org/jobs. Start date as soon as possible.

The American Enterprise Institute (AEI) seeks a full-time, in-person research assistant to work with two China studies senior fellows, Derek Scissors and Dan Blumenthal. This role focuses on issues related to Chinese corporations and Chinese foreign policy, U.S.-China competition, Chinese macroeconomics, Indo-Pacific security and economic relations, and U.S. strategy in the Indo-Pacific. Washington, DC (fully onsite). Salary $50,000–$54,000.

Key responsibilities include: researching, editing, and assisting in publishing policy reports about economics, international trade, authoritarian governance, security, and politics in the Indo-Pacific; helping update the China Global Investment Tracker through data collection, in-depth research in Chinese, fact-checking, editing, and data visualization; helping plan, organize, and coordinate major public and private conferences and private meetings; coordinating program activities and administrative details including managing schedules, setting up meetings with foreign contacts, and planning travel logistics; managing long-term projects by drafting proposals, mapping timelines, organizing small working groups, editing longer publications, and reporting on project progress to the Development department; complying with the Foreign and Defense Policy department’s reporting guidelines and assisting with department events; and mentoring Asia economics and security interns.

Qualifications: a bachelor’s degree in East Asian studies, international relations, political science, history, public policy, or a related field; 0–2 years of previous applicable full-time work experience (previous internship experience strongly preferred); working proficiency in Mandarin Chinese required; previous economics coursework preferred; proficiency in Microsoft Excel required; and excellent research, writing, editing, organizational, and interpersonal skills. Stata a plus. Background in Chinese economy, political economy, politics, or security preferred.

Compensation and logistics: salary $50,000–$54,000. Generous AEI benefits including 18 days paid leave, 12 days paid sick leave, paid family leave, medical and dental, HSA, FSA, tuition assistance up to $5,200, life and disability insurance at no cost, and 403(b) retirement plan. Fully onsite, Washington, DC. Apply at aei.org/jobs with resume, cover letter, transcripts, and 500-word writing sample.

item.title: Senior Policy Analyst – Child Welfare (Federal Advocacy)
item.description:
⚠️ This position is funded through September 29, 2027; future employment is contingent on available funding. Phone interviews began November 16, 2026 — apply immediately. All applications must include resume, cover letter, AND writing sample to be considered.

Note: 3–5 years of relevant experience required; Capitol Hill experience strongly preferred. Salary low $80,000s to low $90,000s. Washington, DC Metro Area (hybrid). Requires living in the DC metropolitan area. Master’s degree preferred; relevant experience considered in lieu of higher education. The ZERO TO THREE Policy Center is urgently hiring; phone interviews began November 16.

The ZERO TO THREE Policy Center is a nonpartisan, research-based resource for policymakers and advocates on the unique developmental needs of infants and toddlers. ZERO TO THREE seeks a Senior Policy Analyst, Child Welfare to play a key role in developing and promoting child welfare issues related to ZERO TO THREE’s comprehensive federal and state policy agenda. The position is also integral to the Safe Babies™ Program, which supports states and communities in building a more coordinated and aligned early childhood system to keep families together by igniting collective action to meet the urgent needs of babies, toddlers, and their families. Washington, DC Metro Area (hybrid). Salary low $80,000s to low $90,000s.

Key responsibilities include (Policy Strategy and Implementation): developing and implementing strategies to advance ZERO TO THREE’s federal child welfare policy agenda, working with internal teams, external consultants, and partners; advancing policies and investments that prioritize the social, emotional, and cognitive needs of infants and toddlers, support caregivers and educators, address trauma, prevent family separation, and promote safe, stable environments; and ensuring cross-team collaboration integrating equity-centered policy solutions. (Policy Expertise and Analysis): demonstrating deep knowledge of child welfare prevention and early childhood education policy including CAPTA, Title IVB, Family First Prevention Services Act, and other federal programs supporting children and families in the child welfare system; providing real-time analysis of the political landscape; identifying legislative champions; and working with the Safe Babies policy team to ensure legislative positions fully reflect ZERO TO THREE’s values and commitment to racial equity. (Communication and Collaboration): building and maintaining strategic relationships with Congressional staff, Administration officials, and coalition partners; providing technical assistance to federal policymakers; writing policy briefs, testimony, report language, blog posts, and updates for a variety of audiences including Congress, the Administration, and advocates; and organizing Congressional briefings, webinars, and meetings.

Qualifications: minimum 3–5 years of relevant work experience; Capitol Hill experience strongly preferred; knowledge of legislative and regulatory processes; broad knowledge of child welfare policy issues at the state and federal levels; strong interpersonal and communication skills; ability to work effectively in culturally diverse environments; exceptional reasoning, problem-solving, and strategic thinking skills; experience participating in coalition groups and building relationships with relevant partners. Bachelor’s degree required; master’s preferred.

Compensation and logistics: salary low $80,000s to low $90,000s. Comprehensive ZERO TO THREE benefits including medical, dental, vision, HRA, retirement contributions, and generous leave. Hybrid in Washington, DC Metro Area. Position funded through September 29, 2027. Apply via Greenhouse with resume, cover letter, AND writing sample.

item.title: Policy Advocate – Virginia Clean Energy & Climate (Southeast Regional Team)
item.description:
Note: IMPORTANT — This is a 2-year limited-term position. 4–7 years of work experience related to environment, climate, or energy policy required. Salary $117,000–$130,000. Must be based in Virginia (Richmond or Charlottesville area preferred). Hybrid: 8 days per month in-office at a Virginia location; travel to Richmond and other NRDC U.S. offices required. Willing to register as a state lobbyist required. Unionized position (The Washington Baltimore News Guild / WBNG CWA Local 32035). Apply at nrdc.org/careers with resume and cover letter.

The Natural Resources Defense Council (NRDC) is an international nonprofit environmental organization with more than 3 million members and online activists. NRDC seeks a Policy Advocate for its Southeast Regional team of the Climate and Energy Program, committed to transitioning the southern economy to clean energy by addressing environmental and energy inequities through partnership, building the environmental movement, and advocating for ambitious, effective policies. This is a 2-year limited-term position based in Virginia. Salary $117,000–$130,000.

Key responsibilities include: supporting the development and advancement of a broad portfolio of equitable climate and clean energy policies including power sector decarbonization, energy efficiency, renewable energy, transportation and building electrification, and industrial decarbonization; building partnerships and collaborating with state clean energy coalitions and a network of allies including environmental justice organizations, frontline and community groups, utility groups, consumer and low-income advocates, labor, the faith community, and clean energy businesses; developing and nurturing durable partnerships with state and local decision makers and elected officials; conducting research, analysis, and design of state and local climate and clean energy policies including utility regulatory policy; providing written and oral advocacy at state agencies, the state legislature, and the governor’s office; representing NRDC at conferences and serving as a spokesperson in the press; and collaborating with internal teams of campaign, communications, public engagement, and policy experts.

Qualifications: bachelor’s degree required; law degree, master’s, or other advanced degree preferred; 4–7 years of work experience related to environment, climate, energy policy, or a related field; experience in state-level clean energy and climate advocacy; experience navigating diverse stakeholders and building consensus; experience building and cultivating relationships within administrative, regulatory, or legislative fora; experience intervening in utility commission and related regulatory proceedings preferable; willingness to register as a state lobbyist; must be based in Virginia. Salary $117,000–$130,000.

Compensation and logistics: salary $117,000–$130,000. Comprehensive NRDC benefits including premium healthcare, generous time off (including year-end Rest & Recharge Week), 403(b) with employer match, and parental leave. 2-year limited-term position. Virginia-based (hybrid, 8 days/month in-office). Unionized position. Apply at nrdc.org/careers.

item.title: Senior Policy Analyst – Early Childhood Care & Education / Maternal Health
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 12/1/2026.

Note: Minimum 3 years of experience in state-level policy advocacy required. Salary $68,000–$74,000. Richmond, VA (hybrid — required in-office Wednesdays; additional in-person days during Virginia General Assembly session). Must live in Richmond or within reasonable commuting distance; this is not a fully remote position. Applications reviewed on a rolling basis starting October 11, 2026 — apply promptly.

Voices for Virginia’s Children is a statewide policy advocacy organization working to improve outcomes for all Virginia children. Voices seeks a Senior Policy Analyst to drive statewide, systems-level change with a focus on Early Childhood Care & Education (ECE) and Maternal Health policy. The role focuses on the policies and systems that support families during pregnancy, the postpartum period, and a child’s earliest years, recognizing the deep connections among parents’ health and well-being, access to high-quality and affordable child care, and healthy child development. Issues covered include reducing maternal mortality rates, reducing racial disparities in perinatal health outcomes, improving maternal and infant mental health care, expanding access to affordable child care, and fairly compensating early educators. Richmond, VA (hybrid). Salary $68,000–$74,000.

Key responsibilities include (Policy Advocacy and Leadership): leading Voices’ policy work in ECE and maternal health; monitoring legislative and administrative developments; analyzing policy and research; identifying opportunities for systems change; developing evidence-based policy recommendations; and having primary responsibility for advancing these issue areas during Virginia’s General Assembly session. (Community Relationship Building): leading and participating in coalitions within the focus area; serving as the main Voices liaison for partner organizations; providing technical assistance to partner coalitions and state workgroups; and working in partnership with the Director of Engagement and Virginia’s Youth in Action (VAYA) members to center youth voice and lived expertise. (Strategic Communications): working with the Communications Manager on policy briefs, one-pagers, blogs, and other advocacy materials; and conducting trainings and presentations on education and advocacy related to issue areas. (Racial Equity): promoting racial equity across all dimensions of work and assessing policies for their impact on all races.

Qualifications: strong verbal and written communication with public speaking confidence; minimum 3 years of experience working in state-level policy advocacy with knowledge and understanding of the Virginia state legislative process; ability to build relationships with legislators, community members, partner organizations, and other stakeholders; ability to effectively analyze data and research to identify trends and inform policymaking; and strong commitment to social, economic, and racial justice with active centering of equity and inclusion. Preferred: highly organized, motivated, and detail-oriented; experience with media or communications; experience with community engagement. Candidates are encouraged to apply even without meeting every requirement.

Compensation and logistics: salary $68,000–$74,000 (organization typically hires at or below mid-range to preserve salary growth). Excellent health insurance with fully covered health, dental, and vision employee premiums; FSA; 30 days PTO + 12 paid holidays; paid parental leave; 3% retirement contribution; professional development stipend; monthly remote work stipend. Richmond, VA (hybrid). Apply via Voices for Virginia’s Children website.

item.title: Family Navigator Coordinator – Virginia (Charlottesville/Richmond)
item.description:
Note: Position end date September 30, 2027 (grant-funded). Salary $26.78–$31.00/hour. Charlottesville, VA and Richmond, VA (hybrid). Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle required. 2–3 years of relevant professional experience strongly preferred. Fluency in English required; additional language proficiency (Spanish, Dari, Farsi, and/or Pashto) desired. OPEIU union position.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. The IRC Virginia office seeks a Family Navigator Coordinator to support IRC clients in building stability and eliminating identified barriers to allow clients to gain employment and achieve long-term self-sufficiency. The Coordinator works closely with colleagues across IRC programs and external partners to ensure clients have the knowledge and resources they need to thrive in their community. This role focuses on maintaining and building strong partnerships and referral pathways within the community and coordinating education opportunities through workshops and orientations for clients to learn how to access and utilize essential services. Charlottesville and Richmond, VA (hybrid). Salary $26.78–$31.00/hour.

Key responsibilities include (Family Support): identifying and maintaining a resource list for clients including free or low-cost healthcare options; providing tailored referral support for clients seeking healthcare resources within the community; coordinating initial health screenings; adapting and vetting culturally appropriate health education materials and educational workshops to build health system literacy and address health-related barriers to employment and self-sufficiency; coordinating initial school enrollment appointments and maintaining positive school relationships; and collaborating with internal and external partners to access services for early childhood applications, advocacy for services for children, parent engagement, educational workshops, and other community resources that support long-term stability. (Partnership Building): maintaining and strengthening partnerships within established program priorities; and attending partner meetings as directed, representing IRC within the scope of assigned tasks.

Qualifications: undergraduate degree or equivalent experience; relevant professional experience in human services, health navigation, education, youth programming, or nonprofit program required (2–3 years strongly preferred); experience with immigrant and refugee populations preferred; lived experience valued; knowledge of Virginia and/or U.S. public benefits, health, or school systems strongly preferred; strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; fluent in English; additional language proficiency in Spanish, Dari, Farsi, and/or Pashto desired; proficient in Microsoft Office applications; valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle required.

Compensation and logistics: salary $26.78–$31.00/hour. Comprehensive IRC benefits including 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20–25 days PTO, medical starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, 403(b) with employer match (immediate vesting), and EAP. Grant-funded position ending September 30, 2027. Charlottesville and Richmond, VA (hybrid). Valid driver’s license required. OPEIU union position.

The White House Fellows Program is one of America’s most prestigious programs for leadership and public service. Founded in 1964, the program has a nonpartisan tradition and has operated under both Republican and Democratic administrations. White House Fellows are selected by the President’s Commission on White House Fellowships to serve for one year in paid federal service working with a senior government principal, with an educational program complementing the placement through discussions with leaders and study of public policy in practice. Applications for the 2027–2028 class are open. Application deadline January 14, 2027.

The selection process is competitive. Former Fellows screen applications to identify the most promising candidates, and the most qualified applicants are selected to be interviewed by regional panels. Approximately 30 candidates proceed as National Finalists; the President’s Commission then interviews and recommends 11–19 outstanding candidates for a one-year presidential appointment. National Finalists are subject to investigation and verification by accredited federal investigators. Fellows must be eligible to obtain a top-secret security clearance.

The application consists of three parts: Part 1 (personal information, contact details, eligibility information, current employment, declarations); Part 2 (education, employment, and civic/volunteer experience; six essays covering current employment (200 words), most significant professional achievement (200 words), most significant community service achievement (200 words), lifetime goals (300 words), motivation for becoming a White House Fellow (300 words), and a 500-word memorandum for the President); and Part 3 (three letters of recommendation, with an optional fourth). Fellows receive a competitive federal salary, are eligible for Federal Employee Health Benefits, and are responsible for their own housing arrangements in Washington, DC.
